runner: work/dpg-proof/run.mjs (previously accepted; unchanged in this review)
scope: Prepared scenario source and local runner compatibility only; no PostgreSQL, browser, host or provider action

findings.evidence: The mobile scenario waits for visible text inside #events. In the frozen Loom page, #events is nested inside <details id=inspect> without an open attribute. Its contents are hidden until the summary is activated, and Playwright waitFor defaults to visible. The desktop #events-desktop check can pass, but the mobile check will time out regardless of a successfully persisted event.
findings.repair: Open #inspect through its visible summary or set its open state through a user-equivalent interaction before waiting for the mobile event, then capture the mobile inspector in the screenshot. Assert the details is open and the event row is visible.

findings.evidence: The script checks only that #notice is not equal to the positive closure sentence. That can pass for UNKNOWN or another unavailable notice. The fixture intends an open, connected, uncertified mission.
findings.repair: Assert the exact open notice and/or authenticated Loom projection closed=false with state=available, and retain its response in controlled evidence. Do not infer completion from the screenshot or from inequality alone.

reviewedBoundaries: The scenario checks the exact clean source SHA, uses the accepted runner's five C4_PG variables, connects to the runner's owned PostgreSQL database, invokes the canonical migrator and production SQL mission/governor APIs, and binds the HTTP server to ephemeral loopback.

The progress fixture is typed v1 started, with approved strategy/check, exact lease and plan/policy digests, zero usage and no provider call; its durable event label matches Loom projection's Governor decision recorded mapping.
The owner session cookie and unauthenticated 401 check fit the current server route. Desktop selectors #live, #objective, #events-desktop and #refresh-desktop exist in frozen source.
The installed Playwright chromium.executablePath() resolves to the known bundled Chromium path, and the file exists. No browser was launched during review.
The runner has a 240-second scenario deadline, owns only its disposable loopback PostgreSQL cluster, and checks its marker/PID before stop. Scenario finally closes browser, HTTP server and pools.
limits: This is not runtime evidence. No PostgreSQL, browser, host or provider operation was performed.
No builder execution, certification, integration, delivery or live publication is established by the proposed proof.
direction: One bounded scenario-only repair for mobile inspector visibility and exact open-state assertion, then rehash, syntax-check, independent delta review and a single owned local run through the accepted runner.
